groups.name: SCALES
groups.why: Five-note, twelve-note, all-whole-steps, and the blues scale. DIMINISHED and AUGMENTED name real scales too, but they are needed in the chord group.

groups.name: MINOR-3RD MODES
groups.why: Each has a flat 3rd above its tonic. Ionian, Lydian and Mixolydian are the major-3rd modes.

groups.name: CHORD QUALITIES
groups.why: Augmented = major 3rd + sharp 5. Diminished = flat 3 + flat 5. Sus = the 3rd swapped for a 2nd or 4th. Dominant 7 = major triad + flat 7. MAJOR is a quality too, but it enlisted.

groups.name: ARMY WORDS TOO
groups.why: A major is a rank and a key. A march is a step and a genre. Taps and Reveille are the bugle calls for lights-out and wake-up.

groups.name: TEMPOS
groups.why: Allegro = fast and lively, andante = walking pace, adagio = slow, presto = very fast. ALLEGRO was also a 1970s Austin car, but the tempos need it.

groups.name: DYNAMICS
groups.why: Piano = soft, forte = loud, crescendo = get louder, diminuendo = get softer. FORTE is also a Kia, but the dynamics need it.

groups.name: PIECE TYPES
groups.why: A study, a night piece, a piece whose theme keeps coming back, and a dance in 3. SONATA and PRELUDE are piece types too, but they are parked in the garage.

groups.name: CAR NAMES
groups.why: Hyundai Sonata, Honda Prelude, Kia Cadenza and Honda Jazz. Carmakers love a music word.

groups.name: NOTE VALUES
groups.why: Whole, half, quarter, eighth: each lasts half as long as the one before. EIGHTH hides the number EIGHT, but it is too honest to count as hidden.

groups.name: VOICE TYPES
groups.why: Choir voices from high to low. TENOR and BARITONE are voices too, but they are smuggling numbers.

groups.name: TWOS
groups.why: Dyad = two-note chord, duplet = two notes in the time of three, duet = a piece for two, duple meter = two beats a bar. HALF is one of two halves, but it is a note value.

groups.name: HIDDEN NUMBERS
groups.why: TENor, bariTONE hides ONE (bariT-ONE), TENuto, xylophONE. Count the letters, not the beats.

groups.name: FRETTED INSTRUMENTS
groups.why: Metal frets across the neck mark each half step. A violin has a neck but no frets.

groups.name: KEYBOARD INSTRUMENTS
groups.why: All played from a keyboard. The celesta is the bell sound in the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy.

groups.name: PIANO PARTS
groups.why: Press the key, the damper lifts, the hammer hits the string, and three legs hold it all up. KEY, HAMMER and LEG are sports words too (the key in basketball, the hammer throw, a relay leg), but the piano needs all four.

groups.name: ALSO SPORTS WORDS
groups.why: Pitch: a note's highness or a throw. Run: a fast scale or a score. Slide: a guitar slide or into second. Hit: a chart smash or a single to left.

groups.name: SOLFEGE
groups.why: Do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti. RAY and ME are real solfege spellings too (the old English tonic sol-fa: doh, ray, me), but they are puns in the song.

groups.name: NOTES OF G♭ MAJOR
groups.why: G♭ major has six flats: G♭ A♭ B♭ C♭ D♭ E♭ F. C♭ is in this key too, spelled C♭ and never B, but it has a white-key job.

groups.name: SHARPS AND FLATS ON WHITE KEYS
groups.why: E♯ = F, B♯ = C, F♭ = E, C♭ = B. You meet E♯ in F♯ major and C♭ in G♭ major.

groups.name: DO-RE-MI PUNS
groups.why: From the Sound of Music song: doe a deer, ray a drop of golden sun, me a name I call myself, far a long way to run.

groups.name: DIATONIC 7THS IN C MAJOR
groups.why: In C: G7 = V7, Bø7 = viiø7, Fmaj7 = IVmaj7, Dm7 = ii7. Fmaj7 and Dm7 also live in F major (Imaj7 and vi7), but F already has four of its own.

groups.name: DIATONIC 7THS IN G MAJOR
groups.why: In G: D7 = V7, F♯ø7 = viiø7, Gmaj7 = Imaj7, Em7 = vi7. Em7 is iii7 in C too, but C is full.

groups.name: DIATONIC 7THS IN F MAJOR
groups.why: In F: C7 = V7, Eø7 = viiø7, Gm7 = ii7, B♭maj7 = IVmaj7. Every vii here is ø7, never °7: a half-diminished chord has a minor 7th on top.

groups.name: SOUNDS LIKE ANOTHER WORD
groups.why: Chord/cord, root/route, time/thyme, rest/wrest.

groups.name: VIOLIN BOW PARTS
groups.why: The frog is the end you hold, the tip is the far end, the stick is the wooden shaft and the hair is horsehair, rosined. GRIP and HEAD are bow parts too (the leather grip; the head is another name for the tip), but they golf.

groups.name: ORNAMENTS
groups.why: Trill = rapid alternation with the note above. Mordent = a quick flick to a neighbor and back. Turn = above, note, below, note. Appoggiatura = a leaning note that steals time.

groups.name: BRITISH NOTE NAMES
groups.why: UK names: semibreve = whole note, minim = half, crotchet = quarter, quaver = eighth.

groups.name: ALSO GOLF WORDS
groups.why: Swing is a jazz feel, a hook is the catchy bit, grip is how you hold the sticks or the bow, and the head is a jazz tune's main melody. TURN is golf too (the turn after nine holes), but it is an ornament.

groups.name: PARENT KEY: C MAJOR
groups.why: All white keys. Counted from C, G Mixolydian's home chord is V, F Lydian's is IV, D Dorian's is ii and E Phrygian's is iii.

groups.name: PARENT KEY: G MAJOR
groups.why: Every one uses F♯. C Lydian's raised 4th is that F♯. A Dorian's home chord is ii in G, never i.

groups.name: MODES WITH A MINOR 3RD
groups.why: All flat-3 modes, and all four come from F major (one B♭). D DORIAN, E PHRYGIAN and A DORIAN have minor 3rds too, but their parent keys need them.

groups.name: RELATIVE ___
groups.why: Relative minor, relative major, relative pitch, relative key. It is the Parent Trap, so the family words win.

groups.name: DRUM KIT
groups.why: Snare drum, hi-hat, ride cymbal and crash cymbal: standard drum kit gear.

groups.name: DRUMMERS PLAY WITH
groups.why: Sticks, wire brushes, soft mallets and bundled rods: four ways to hit a drum. MALLETS live in a toolbox too.

groups.name: INSIDE A PIANO
groups.why: Felt hammers strike steel piano wire, dampers stop it, and the soundboard makes it loud. HAMMER and WIRE live in a toolbox too.

groups.name: ALSO IN A TOOLBOX
groups.why: A guitar pick, a musical saw played with a bow, recording tape, and sandpaper blocks from the rhythm band.

groups.name: PROPERTIES OF SOUND
groups.why: How high, what color, how long, how loud: the four things your ear measures in every note.

groups.name: RHYTHM WORDS
groups.why: Beat = the steady unit, tempo = its speed, meter = how beats group, pulse = the heartbeat under it all. BEAT also sounds like beet, but the homophone group is all instruments.

groups.name: PLUCKED STRINGS
groups.why: All plucked. LYRE and LUTE are plucked strings too, but they had another job.

groups.name: INSTRUMENTS WITH A SOUNDALIKE
groups.why: Cymbal/symbol, lyre/liar, bell/belle, lute/loot.

groups.name: PERFECT INTERVALS
groups.why: Unison, 4th, 5th and octave are the perfect intervals. The tritone sits between the 4th and 5th and is not perfect.

groups.name: MAJOR-OR-MINOR INTERVALS
groups.why: 2nds, 3rds, 6ths and 7ths come in major and minor. SECOND is also a unit of time, but here it is a step.

groups.name: KINDS OF MINOR
groups.why: Harmonic, melodic and natural minor scales, and the relative minor that shares a major key's notes. NATURAL is also an accidental.

groups.name: PERFECT ___
groups.why: Perfect pitch, perfect cadence (V to I), perfect score, perfect harmony. UNISON, FOURTH, FIFTH and OCTAVE all take PERFECT too, but they are the intervals.

groups.name: MAJOR TRIADS
groups.why: Major 3rd on the bottom, minor 3rd on top. D major needs F♯.

groups.name: MINOR TRIADS
groups.why: Minor 3rd on the bottom, major 3rd on top. G minor needs B♭. A·C·E, B·E·G and F·A·D are minor triads too, but they spell words.

groups.name: DIMINISHED TRIADS
groups.why: Two stacked minor 3rds. B-D-F is the vii° chord in C major. Flat the B in E-G-B and it turns diminished.

groups.name: CHORDS THAT SPELL WORDS
groups.why: A·C·E = A minor (vi in C). B·E·G = E minor with B on the bottom. F·A·D = D minor with F on the bottom. F·A·C·E = Fmaj7, and the treble-clef spaces.

groups.name: LATIN DANCES
groups.why: Tango (Argentina), samba (Brazil), rumba and mambo (Cuba). SALSA and the Cuban BOLERO are Latin dances too, but they have other homes.

groups.name: DANCES IN 3/4
groups.why: All triple meter. The Spanish bolero is in 3/4, and so is Ravel's Boléro.

groups.name: DRUM RUDIMENTS
groups.why: Flam = one grace note before the main stroke. Paradiddle = R L R R, L R L L. Drag and ruff = two grace notes before the stroke. ROLL is a rudiment too, but it is on the menu.

groups.name: ALSO ON THE MENU
groups.why: Salsa the genre, a jam session, a drum roll, and the shake, the old English name for a trill. Also a dip, a spread, bread and a milkshake.

groups.name: ARTICULATIONS
groups.why: Staccato = short and detached, legato = smooth and connected, tenuto = hold it full value, marcato = marked and strong.

groups.name: ROAD-MAP MARKINGS
groups.why: Da capo = back to the top, dal segno = back to the sign, segno = the sign itself, coda = the tail-end section. FINE is a road-map word too, but it has an English meaning.

groups.name: TEMPO MARKINGS
groups.why: Largo = broad, lento = slow, adagio = at ease, larghetto = a little less slow than largo. GRAVE and PRESTO are tempos too, but they double as English words.

groups.name: ALSO ENGLISH, NEW MEANING
groups.why: Fine = the end (fee-nay), not OK. Grave = very slow and solemn, not a burial. Forte = loud, not your strong suit. Presto = very fast, not a magic word.

groups.name: BAROQUE COMPOSERS
groups.why: Roughly 1600 to 1750: Bach, Handel, Vivaldi (The Four Seasons) and Purcell, England's Baroque star.

groups.name: CLASSICAL-ERA COMPOSERS
groups.why: Roughly 1750 to 1820: Haydn, Mozart, Gluck (who reformed opera) and Beethoven, who started here and opened the door to the Romantics.

groups.name: ROMANTIC COMPOSERS
groups.why: The 1800s: big feelings, big pianos. BEETHOVEN and FIELD fit here too, but the other groups need them.

groups.name: COMPOSERS WHO ARE ALSO WORDS
groups.why: John Cage, Philip Glass, John Field (the Irishman who invented the nocturne) and John Blow (Purcell's teacher, Baroque).

groups.name: JAZZ TRUMPETERS
groups.why: Louis Armstrong, Miles Davis, Dizzy Gillespie and Wynton Marsalis. Chet BAKER played trumpet too, but his name is a job.

groups.name: JAZZ SAXOPHONISTS
groups.why: Charlie Parker, John Coltrane, Sonny Rollins and Stan Getz.

groups.name: JAZZ NOBILITY
groups.why: Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Lady Day (Billie Holiday) and King Oliver, Louis Armstrong's mentor. All four are plain words too, but they hold titles.

groups.name: JAZZ NAMES THAT ARE ALSO WORDS
groups.why: Thelonious Monk (piano), Buddy Rich (drums), Horace Silver (piano) and Chet Baker (trumpet).

groups.name: BEATLES ALBUMS
groups.why: Rubber Soul (1965), Revolver (1966), Abbey Road (1969), Let It Be (1970). YELLOW SUBMARINE was an album too (1969), but it has a color to show off.

groups.name: ROLLING STONES SONGS
groups.why: (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction (1965), Wild Horses (1971), Angie (1973), Start Me Up (1981). PAINT IT BLACK and RUBY TUESDAY are Stones too, but they are colorful.

groups.name: BEATLES SONGS, NO ALBUM TITLE
groups.why: Famous Beatles songs, none of them an album title. Blackbird has a color in it, but it stays with the Beatles.

groups.name: COLOR IN THE TITLE
groups.why: Black, ruby, yellow and purple: two Stones songs, a Beatles song, and Prince's 1984 title track.

groups.name: MOTOWN SOLO STARS
groups.why: All recorded for Motown labels. Mary Wells took My Guy to No. 1 in 1964. RICK JAMES and SMOKEY ROBINSON were Motown solo stars too, but they hide music words.

groups.name: MOTOWN GROUPS
groups.why: Motown groups. Smokey Robinson fronted the Miracles before going solo. The CONTOURS were Motown too.

groups.name: DETROIT STARS, NEVER ON MOTOWN
groups.why: Aretha Franklin grew up in Detroit but recorded for Columbia and then Atlantic. Eminem, Jack White and Alice Cooper are Detroit too, nowhere near Motown. So is KID ROCK, from north of the city.

groups.name: CONTAINS A MUSIC WORD
groups.why: rick JAMes, conTOURs, smoKEY robinson, kid ROCK.

groups.name: COUNTRY STARS
groups.why: Reba McEntire, Dolly Parton, Shania Twain and Zac Brown, whose Zac Brown Band took Chicken Fried to No. 1 country in 2008.

groups.name: JAM BANDS
groups.why: Long songs, longer solos, no two shows alike: the Grateful Dead, Phish, the Allman Brothers Band and the Dave Matthews Band.

groups.name: GRATEFUL DEAD SONGS
groups.why: Bertha (1971), Ripple and Truckin' (1970) and Althea (1980).

groups.name: ___ BAND
groups.why: Brass band, cover band, garage band, marching band. ZAC BROWN, ALLMAN BROTHERS and DAVE MATTHEWS all go before BAND too, but they have other homes.

groups.name: TOTO SONGS
groups.why: Hold the Line (1978), Rosanna and Africa (1982), Pamela (1988). Their 1979 song 99 had a second job.

groups.name: SWEDISH POP ACTS
groups.why: Roxette, Europe (The Final Countdown), Ace of Base and Robyn. ABBA is Swedish too, but it reads the same both ways.

groups.name: STEELY DAN ALBUMS
groups.why: Pretzel Logic (1974), Katy Lied (1975), The Royal Scam (1976), Gaucho (1980). AJA (1977) is Steely Dan too.

groups.name: PALINDROMES
groups.why: Aja (Steely Dan), ABBA, SOS (ABBA, 1975) and 99 (Toto, 1979) all read the same backward.

groups.name: PIANO MAKERS
groups.why: Four piano brands: Steinway (New York and Hamburg), Yamaha and Kawai (Japan), Baldwin (Ohio-born).

groups.name: SINGER-PIANISTS
groups.why: Billy Joel, Alicia Keys, Elton John and Nat King Cole. Carole KING sings at the piano too, but she is on the chessboard.

groups.name: JAZZ PIANO GIANTS
groups.why: Thelonious Monk, Bill Evans, Art Tatum, Herbie Hancock. Nat King COLE and Walter BISHOP Jr. were jazz pianists too, but the other groups need them.

groups.name: CHESS PIECES
groups.why: Carole King, Queen, Gladys Knight and Walter Bishop Jr., Charlie Parker's pianist.

groups.name: ROLLING STONES
groups.why: Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Charlie Watts and Brian Jones, who founded the band.

groups.name: AMERICAN COMPOSERS
groups.why: Aaron Copland (no E), George Gershwin, Leonard Bernstein, Charles Ives.

groups.name: ROCK DRUMMERS
groups.why: John Bonham (Led Zeppelin), Keith Moon (The Who), Neil Peart (Rush), Stewart Copeland (The Police). WATTS drummed for the Stones and Kenney JONES replaced Moon in The Who, but the Stones need both names. Copeland also writes film scores and operas.

groups.name: DRUM ___
groups.why: Drum solo, drum roll, drumbeat, drumline.

groups.name: TAYLOR SWIFT SONGS
groups.why: Love Story (2008), Shake It Off and Blank Space (2014), Anti-Hero (2022). BETTY (2020) and HONEY (2025) are Taylor songs too, but they have other homes.

groups.name: SONGS TITLED JUST A WOMAN'S NAME
groups.why: The Police, Dolly Parton, Derek and the Dominos, and Taylor Swift's betty from folklore.

groups.name: US ONE-HIT WONDERS
groups.why: Los del Rio, Toni Basil, Soft Cell and Dexys Midnight Runners: each act's one giant US hit.

groups.name: HIDDEN ONE
groups.why: alONE (Heart, 1987), hONEy (Mariah Carey, 1997, and Taylor Swift, 2025), lONEly (Akon, 2005), mONEy (Pink Floyd, 1973). Squash the spaces in COME ON EILEEN and you get comeONEileen, but it is a one-hit wonder.

groups.name: BANDS WITH NUMBERS
groups.why: Numbers in the name: U2, Maroon 5, Sum 41 and Boyz II Men (a Roman two). THREE DOG NIGHT has a number too, but it went to the zoo.

groups.name: BANDS NAMED FOR PLACES
groups.why: Two cities and two states. ARCTIC MONKEYS name a place too, but they went to the zoo.

groups.name: ANIMAL BANDS, SPELLED RIGHT
groups.why: The Eagles, The Turtles, Three Dog Night (Joy to the World, 1971) and Arctic Monkeys (Sheffield, 2002). Proper spelling.

groups.name: BANDS SPELLED WRONG ON PURPOSE
groups.why: Beetles with a beat, Monkeys with double E, Birds with a Y, Gorillas with a Z. BOYZ II MEN misspell boys too, but they count.

groups.name: JOHN WILLIAMS SCORES
groups.why: Two notes of shark, a flying hero, a boy wizard and a phone-home alien. STAR WARS is Williams too, but it has a sky word.

groups.name: HENRY MANCINI TUNES
groups.why: Peter Gunn (1958), Baby Elephant Walk (from Hatari!), The Pink Panther and Charade (1963). MOON RIVER is Mancini too.

groups.name: OSCAR-WINNING SONGS
groups.why: Fame (1980), Shallow (A Star Is Born), Lose Yourself (8 Mile, the first rap winner) and White Christmas (Holiday Inn, 1942). MOON RIVER, SKYFALL and OVER THE RAINBOW won too, but they have sky words.

groups.name: SKY WORD INSIDE
groups.why: STAR Wars, MOON River, SKYfall and Over the RAINBOW.

groups.name: MUSIC FESTIVALS
groups.why: California, Chicago, England, and Newport, Rhode Island, where Dylan went electric in 1965. BONNAROO and STAGECOACH are festivals too, but they are hiding animals.

groups.name: PLAYED WOODSTOCK, 1969
groups.why: Janis Joplin, Joan Baez, The Who and Creedence Clearwater Revival. HENDRIX and SANTANA played too, but they are hiding animals.

groups.name: SKIPPED WOODSTOCK, 1969
groups.why: Bob Dylan lived near the town of Woodstock, NY, and still skipped it. The Doors and Led Zeppelin turned it down. Joni Mitchell stayed in New York for The Dick Cavett Show and wrote the song Woodstock instead.

groups.name: HIDDEN ANIMAL
groups.why: HENdrix, sANTana, bonnaROO, STAGecoach: a hen, an ant, a kangaroo and a stag.

groups.name: OPERA TITLE ROLES
groups.why: Four Verdi operas named for their main character. FIGARO (Mozart) and BUTTERFLY (Puccini) are title roles too, but they are hiding snacks.

groups.name: SYMPHONY NICKNAMES
groups.why: Haydn 94 (Surprise), Mozart 41 (Jupiter), Beethoven 3 (Eroica), Dvorak 9 (From the New World).

groups.name: BEETHOVEN PIANO SONATA NICKNAMES
groups.why: Op. 27 No. 2 (Moonlight), Op. 57 (Appassionata), Op. 53 (Waldstein), Op. 31 No. 2 (Tempest). HAMMERKLAVIER (Op. 106) is one too, but it is hiding a ham.

groups.name: HIDDEN FOOD
groups.why: BUTTERfly (Puccini's Madama Butterfly), NUTcracker (Tchaikovsky), FIGaro (Mozart), HAMmerklavier (Beethoven).

groups.name: SONGS WITH A DAY
groups.why: The Bangles, the Rolling Stones, T-Bone Walker (Call It Stormy Monday, 1947) and Maroon 5. STORMY and SUNDAY hide weather too, but the days need them.

groups.name: OPERA TENORS
groups.why: Placido Domingo, Luciano Pavarotti and Jose Carreras (the Three Tenors) plus Enrico Caruso. Domingo is Spanish for Sunday, which is the trap.

groups.name: SONGS WITH A MONTH
groups.why: Earth, Wind & Fire, Guns N' Roses, The Four Seasons (Oh, What a Night) and U2. NOVEMBER RAIN hides weather too.

groups.name: WEATHER INSIDE
groups.why: WINDy (The Association, 1967), SUNny (Bobby Hebb, 1966), SNOWbird (Anne Murray, 1970) and Over the RAINbow.

groups.name: SONGS FROM MOVIE MUSICALS
groups.why: Frozen, The Little Mermaid, Moana, Beauty and the Beast. HELP!, YELLOW SUBMARINE, MAMMA MIA! and GREASE are sung in movie musicals too, but each has another home.

groups.name: BEATLES SONGS
groups.why: All Beatles. Help! and Yellow Submarine were also Beatles movies.

groups.name: BROADWAY SHOWS THAT BECAME MOVIES
groups.why: Stage first, screen second. HAIRSPRAY hides HAIR, but it stays on Broadway.

groups.name: HIDDEN BODY PART
groups.why: EARth Angel (The Penguins), wHIP It (Devo, 1980), SHINy Happy People (R.E.M., 1991), kARMa Chameleon (Culture Club, 1983).

groups.name: BTS SONGS
groups.why: Dynamite (their first all-English single, 2020), Butter (2021), Idol and Fake Love (2018).

groups.name: MAROON 5 SONGS
groups.why: Payphone (2012), Animals (2014), Sugar (from V) and Memories (2019).

groups.name: HARRY STYLES SONGS
groups.why: Sign of the Times (2017), Adore You and Watermelon Sugar (Fine Line, 2019), As It Was (2022).

groups.name: BAKING INGREDIENT INSIDE
groups.why: BUTTERfly (Mariah Carey, 1997), SALT-N-Pepa, Brown SUGAR (Rolling Stones) and HONEY (Mariah Carey). BUTTER, SUGAR and WATERMELON SUGAR bake too, but their artists need them.

groups.name: MUSIC VIDEO GAMES
groups.why: Plastic guitar, full band, tap the black tiles, and slice the beats in VR.

groups.name: MUSIC FORMATS
groups.why: Records, tapes, compact discs and the chunky 8-track cartridge.

groups.name: STREAMING SERVICES
groups.why: All music streaming apps. PANDORA hides PAN, the steel pan of the Caribbean.

groups.name: HIDDEN INSTRUMENT
groups.why: HARPsichord, BASSoon, violonCELLO, flugelHORN. GUITAR HERO, PIANO TILES and PANDORA hide instruments too, but their groups need them.

groups.name: ONE-NAME SINGERS
groups.why: First names or stage names, no last names needed. Cheryl (Fight for This Love, 2009) also hides CHER. ROBYN is a one-name singer too.

groups.name: STAGE SURNAMES FROM OUTER SPACE
groups.why: Bruno Mars, Freddie Mercury, Ringo Starr (two Rs) and Keith Moon.

groups.name: REAL FIRST NAMES: RIHANNA, CHER, ELTON, STING
groups.why: Robyn Fenty, Cherilyn Sarkisian, Reginald Dwight, Gordon Sumner.

groups.name: HIDDEN ONE-NAME SINGER
groups.why: harMONICA, accorDION, sEVEnth, PINK Floyd: Monica, Dion, Eve and P!nk. CHERILYN and CHERYL both hide CHER, but they have other homes.

groups.name: SABRINA CARPENTER SONGS
groups.why: Nonsense and Feather (2022), Espresso and Taste (2024).

groups.name: JUG BAND INSTRUMENTS
groups.why: Kitchen and laundry gear turned band. SPOONS and JUG are kitchenware too.

groups.name: FIRST SONGS PIANO STUDENTS LEARN
groups.why: Three notes, then Beethoven's Ninth, then the holidays, then the duet everyone plays. CHOPSTICKS is kitchenware too.

groups.name: ALSO KITCHENWARE
groups.why: A tuning fork, a major scale, a mixing desk and a steel pan. Also a utensil, a kitchen scale, a stand mixer and a frying pan.

groups.name: SONGS ABOUT CANDY
groups.why: The Chordettes (1958), the Archies (1969), Joey Dee and the Starliters (1961) and the Strangeloves (1965). I WANT CANDY hides an ANT.

groups.name: HITS FROM SUPERHERO MOVIES
groups.why: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, Black Panther, Batman Forever and Tim Burton's Batman (Prince, a 1989 No. 1). BATDANCE hides a BAT.

groups.name: MUSIC NICKNAMES
groups.why: Bruce Springsteen, Elvis Presley, Louis Armstrong (from Satchelmouth) and Charlie Parker. BIRD is an animal too.

groups.name: HIDDEN ANIMAL
groups.why: shAPE of You (Ed Sheeran), rOXanne (The Police), sCATman (Scatman John) and Mrs. ROBINson (Simon & Garfunkel).

groups.name: BROADWAY MUSICALS
groups.why: Hamilton, Wicked, Cats and Camelot (1960). CATS and CAMELOT hide animals too.

groups.name: SONGS FROM ANNIE
groups.why: Tomorrow, Maybe, It's the Hard-Knock Life and Easy Street.

groups.name: NATIONAL MUSIC AWARDS
groups.why: Grammy (USA), Brit (UK), Juno (Canada), ARIA (Australia). GRAMMY hides a RAM.

groups.name: HIDDEN ANIMAL
groups.why: RAMones, HENley (Don Henley of the Eagles), COWbell and jEWEl.

groups.name: VIVALDI'S FOUR SEASONS
groups.why: Vivaldi's four violin concertos. Each tile is a season, so each also contains one, but Vivaldi needs all four.

groups.name: MUSIC BIOPICS
groups.why: Elton John (2019), Ray Charles (2004), Elvis Presley (2022), Johnny Cash (2005). ELVIS was the King, but the biopics need him.

groups.name: ROYAL NICKNAMES
groups.why: King of Pop, Queen of Soul, Queen of Disco, King of Swing. DONNA SUMMER contains a season too.

groups.name: SEASON INSIDE
groups.why: SPRINGsteen, SUMMERtime (Gershwin), AUTUMN Leaves (the jazz standard) and FALLin' (Alicia Keys, 2001).

groups.name: SONGS ABOUT DOGS
groups.why: Elvis (and Big Mama Thornton first), the B-I-N-G-O camp song, Paul McCartney's sheepdog, and Elvis again with Old Shep.

groups.name: ACTS WITH A DOG IN THE NAME
groups.why: A rapper, a 1970s hit machine (Joy to the World, 1971), Chris Cornell's 1991 Seattle supergroup, and the band behind Everything Falls Apart.

groups.name: SPEAKER PARTS
groups.why: Woofer = lows, tweeter = highs, subwoofer = the rumble, crossover = the circuit that splits the sound. WOOFER, SUBWOOFER and TWEETER hide animal sounds too.

groups.name: HIDDEN ANIMAL SOUND
groups.why: gARFunkel, HOWLin' Wolf, sMOOth (Santana, 1999) and HONKy Tonk Women (Rolling Stones, 1969).

groups.name: SONGS STARTING WITH BABY
groups.why: Pinkfong, Raffi, the Supremes and Simon & Garfunkel.

groups.name: PERCUSSION
groups.why: Strike it, shake it, click it, mallet it. Each also contains a percussion instrument, being one.

groups.name: HIT COVERS: SOMEONE ELSE DID IT FIRST
groups.why: Otis Redding (1965) before Aretha (1967), Leonard Cohen before Jeff Buckley, the Top Notes (1961) before the Isley Brothers and the Beatles, Bob Dylan before the Byrds' No. 1. MR. TAMBOURINE MAN hides a TAMBOURINE.

groups.name: HIDDEN PERCUSSION
groups.why: TOMorrow (Annie), jingle BELL rock (Bobby Helms, 1957), RATTLEsnake Shake (Fleetwood Mac, 1969), CHIMEs of Freedom (Bob Dylan, 1964).

groups.name: SONGS AND ALBUMS TITLED WITH A NUMBER
groups.why: Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande, Dolly Parton and Nena. 8 is a Billie Eilish song (2019), 4 is a Beyoncé album (2011) and Adele's albums are numbers too, but they all have other homes.

groups.name: PIANO KEYS, GUITAR STRINGS, STAFF LINES, HALF STEPS IN AN OCTAVE
groups.why: 88 keys on a standard piano, 6 strings on a guitar, 5 lines on a staff, 12 half steps in an octave. 12 is also the twelve-bar blues.

groups.name: ___-BAR
groups.why: A 4-bar phrase, 8-bar blues, 16-bar blues and the 32-bar AABA song form.

groups.name: GUITAR BRANDS
groups.why: Four American guitar makers. MARTIN hides TIN.

groups.name: GUITAR MODELS
groups.why: Fender's Strat and Tele, Gibson's SG and Flying V. LUCILLE and BLACKIE were sold as models too (Gibson's B.B. King Lucille from 1980, Fender's Blackie tribute in 2006).

groups.name: FAMOUS GUITARS WITH NAMES
groups.why: B.B. King's Lucille, Eric Clapton's Blackie, Willie Nelson's Trigger, Eddie Van Halen's Frankenstrat.

groups.name: HIDDEN METAL
groups.why: IRON Maiden, STEELy Dan, LEAD Belly and GOLDfinger (Shirley Bassey, 1964).
